title: A materially ambiguous build prompt -- the agent must ask for the collection-piece identity before building (clarifying-questions stage 2)
//: Member of the 'furnished scene build' family in SHAPE (same bare scaffold, same build-completeness battery) but a DIFFERENT axis under test: the prompt deliberately withholds the collection-piece identity. The setting and mood are intentionally left to ordinary agent judgment, not claimed as scripted-answer adoption. Pairs with the scripted ask_user responder (askUserResponses) to prove the checkpoint battery can distinguish 'asked, then built the answered piece' from 'never asked, built SOMETHING'.
prompts: Build me a display scene for my prized collection piece. Make it look really nice.

checkpointsRationale: TYPE-AGNOSTIC battery + CLARIFICATION-SPECIFIC additions. The first four checkpoints are byte-for-byte the same build-completeness/coherence battery as the build_watch_scene/build_stilllife_scene/build_study_scene family (see those scenarios' own rationale for why it stays type-agnostic) -- they grade whether a coherent, lit, bound scene got built at all, independent of WHAT was built. The trajectory checkpoint's askUserMin/askUserMax/askUserBeforeMutation/askUserQuestionContainsAny and the finalText checkpoint are what make THIS scenario measure clarifying-question behaviour specifically: askUserMin:1 requires the agent to pause rather than silently guessing; askUserMax:3 caps it at the tool's own documented budget (an agent that interrogates the user forever is also failing the task); askUserBeforeMutation:true requires the ask to happen BEFORE the first insert_chunk/insert_chunks/propose_patch/remove_chunk; askUserQuestionContainsAny requires the question itself to concern the collection-piece identity rather than an unrelated detail. The scripted responder intentionally has NO default: a question outside its identity vocabulary receives available:false instead of a misleading pocket-watch answer. The finalText containsAny:["watch","pocket"] then proves the final response reflects the ANSWER the scripted responder gave (a vintage brass pocket watch), not a piece the agent invented independently. The desk/study setting and warm mood in the fixture are chosen by the fixture, not treated as scripted-answer adoption. This scenario MEASURES asking, so its own committed fixture (evals/fixtures/build_ambiguous_scene.fixture.jsonl) must actually ask -- see TestAdversarialControlNeverAsksStillBuilds in tests/AgentEvalCheckTest.cpp for the control that proves a never-asks fixture fails askUserMin specifically while the build checkpoints still pass.
